section.name: EqNotes_WindLoadonPedBridgeSuperstructure_011_C_D
section.paragraph:
Struct_Type
is the selected structure description. The nested If expressions check it in order: girder superstructure gives 1.3; bridge substructure gives 1.6; sharp-edged truss, column, or arch gives 2; the round-member option gives 1. The final fallback branch gives 1.2.
The selected number has no units and multiplies the wind-pressure term. It represents the shape’s drag in the stated model; it is not the structure’s area or a load-combination factor.

report.heading: 3. PRESSURE EXPOSURE AND ELEVATION COEFFICIENT, K_Z ( LRFD Art. 3.8.1.2.1 )
3.1. K_Z for Wind Exposure Category B ( LRFD Eq. 3.8.1.2.1-2 )
report.paragraph: Pressure multiplier for height and Exposure Category B.

section.name: EqNotes_WindLoadonPedBridgeSuperstructure_013_K_Z_B
section.paragraph:
Divide
Z_calc
, the effective height, by 0.9834 ft. The feet cancel so the quantity inside Ln has no units. Ln is the natural logarithm; in this expression it describes how the wind profile changes with height.
Multiply that logarithm by 2.5, then add 6.87. Square the whole quantity in parentheses and divide by 345.6. These constants define the Category B profile used in the displayed equation.
The result is a dimensionless multiplier on pressure. This equation calculates the value for one category; the category-selection equation decides which value is used downstream.

report.paragraph: Reference: LRFD Eq. 3.8.1.2.1-2

Multiply that logarithm by 2.5, then add 7.35. Square the whole quantity in parentheses and divide by 478.4. These constants define the Category C profile used in the displayed equation.
The result is a dimensionless multiplier on pressure. This equation calculates the value for one category; the category-selection equation decides which value is used downstream.

report.heading: 4.4. Service IV applicability — not used
report.paragraph: Service IV is not used in the current nonprestressed pier / steel-pile load set. No Service IV pressure, uplift, or FBMP entry case is produced. Strength III deck uplift remains included.
report.heading: 5. WIND LOADS ON SUPERSTRUCTURE ( LRFD Art. 3.8.1.2.2 AND 3.8.1.2.3a )
report.paragraph: For girder bridges, wind load components on the substructure are determined as the product of skew coefficients ( LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.3a-1 ), the wind pressure from Eq. 3.8.1.2.1-1 , and the depth of the bridge as seen in elevation perpendicular to the longitudinal axis. Both transverse and longitudinal components are applied simultaneously at mid-depth of the superstructure ( LRFD Art. 3.8.1.2.3a ).

For usual girder and slab bridges with individual span length not more than 150 ft and maximum height not more than 33.0 ft above low ground or water level, simplified wind load components may be used per LRFD Art. 3.8.1.2.3a : Transverse = 100% of perpendicular load; Longitudinal = 25% of transverse load.
report.heading: 5.1. Skew Coefficients — Girders ( LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.3a-1 )
report.paragraph: Transverse skew coefficient for girders — from LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.3a-1 based on selected skew angle:
Girder wind-angle multiplier for the force component across the bridge.

section.name: EqNotes_WindLoadonPedBridgeSuperstructure_021_C_T_gir
section.paragraph:
Skew_deg_str
is the wind angle selected in plan, measured from straight across the bridge. The nested If expressions select the entered coefficients for 0°, 15°, 30°, and 45°; the last branch supplies the 60° value. In that order, the numbers are 1, 0.88, 0.82, 0.66, and 0.34.

The chosen number scales the perpendicular-wind load into its component across the bridge. Use the across-bridge and along-bridge coefficients for the same angle together; they are not independent load cases.

report.paragraph: Reference: LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.3a-1
Girder wind-angle multiplier for the force component along the bridge.

section.name: EqNotes_WindLoadonPedBridgeSuperstructure_022_C_L_gir
section.paragraph:
Skew_deg_str
is the wind angle selected in plan, measured from straight across the bridge. The nested If expressions select the entered coefficients for 0°, 15°, 30°, and 45°; the last branch supplies the 60° value. In that order, the numbers are 0, 0.12, 0.24, 0.32, and 0.38.

The chosen number scales the perpendicular-wind load into its component along the bridge. Use the across-bridge and along-bridge coefficients for the same angle together; they are not independent load cases.

report.paragraph: Reference: LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.3a-1

P_Z_III

d_super

Multiply by
C_T_gir
, the selected girder angle multiplier, to obtain the component across the bridge. The result is a line load, not yet a complete support reaction.

section.paragraph: For the retained equal bearing-load allocation, take half the maximum-span line load and divide by the beam count from Bridge Geometry_2 Beam. This is the existing load-distribution assumption.
